title: cp
definition: Copy. The command used to copy files or directories from a source location to a destination location.
simpleExplanation: Copy and Paste. You duplicate a file, leaving the original perfectly intact.
realWorldExample: Before editing a dangerous system file, you make a backup by typing `cp config.txt config.txt.backup`. Now you have two identical files.

basic: What happens if the destination file you are copying to already exists?
intermediate: Why does `cp folder1 folder2` throw an 'omitting directory' error?

answers.question: Destination exists?
answers.answer: By default, `cp` will silently overwrite the destination file, destroying whatever was previously there.

answers.question: Why error on folders?
answers.answer: Because `cp` only copies single files by default. To copy an entire directory and all the files inside it, you must use the Recursive flag: `cp -r folder1 folder2`.

tableData.title: Crucial Command Flags
rows: Recursive. Copy directories and their contents.
Verbose. Explain what is being done.
Preserve. Keep original file attributes (time, ownership).
